newsitem.title: USA: Ill. agency okays projects for Allstate bond plan.
newsitem.headline: Ill. agency okays projects for Allstate bond plan.

text.p: Illinois Development Finance Authority on Wednesday gave preliminary approval to three bond issues for social service agencies under an innovative agreement with Allstate Insurance Co, a unit of Allstate Corp.

The projects totaling $8.149 million are the first for the public/private partnership. The board gave unanimous approval to the initial inducement and the state and Allstate must complete discussions of outstanding issues before completing negotiations, IDFA director Bobby Wilkerson said.
Under the program, Allstate has agreed to purchase bonds of social service agencies in Illinois with limited credit enhancement provided by the finance authority.
Without the agreement, the three Chicago social service agencies would not have the financial ability to pursue a bond issue on their own, Wilkerson said.

The board gave preliminary approval to $4.349 million of bonds for the Human Resources Development Institute, $2.3 of bonds for Substance Abuse Services Inc. and $1.5 million of bonds for the Abraham Lincoln Centre.

Under the program, the finance authority assumes a small risk, "because we believe they are important programs," Wilkerson said. It makes it a good credit risk for Allstate and gives the agencies the capital they need, he added.
Final approval of the first projects could come as early as next month, Wilkerson said.

The finance authority also gave preliminary approval to a number of other bond proposals Wednesday, including a combined request of $93.255 million of bonds for a pool of 26 rehabilitiation service providers in Illinois. All but approximately $8 million of the request would be part of a refinancing, Wilkerson noted.
